column1: # *** PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED. NOT A CAPTURE. ***
# Charge radii and radii changes for Bk (Z=97) and Cf (Z=98), computed at
# register 1560 from established material because the measurement cannot be
# made (R 1559: three of four methods need tens of milligrams; the fourth
# gives differences only and has no anchor to calibrate against).
# METHOD, and every step validated where a validation exists:
#  1. Angeli & Marinova's own reference-radius formula, which THEY use for
#     elements lacking experimental R:
#     VALIDATED: reproduces their listed Cm-244 to 0.0000 fm.
#  2. The formula runs LOW at the top of the chart. Residuals against the four
#     MEASURED actinides (Th, U, Pu, Am) are +0.0335 to +0.0694 fm.
#  3. The formula is a function of A ALONE and cannot distinguish Bk-249 from
#     Cf-249. The residual is therefore regressed on Z:
#  4. Differences use the per-neutron slope measured across 18 adjacent pairs
#     in five elements: 0.0874 +- 0.0213 fm^2 per neutron.
# CONFIDENCE, stated separately because it differs by an order:
#   the ABSOLUTE radii rest on a FOUR-POINT trend with two free parameters.
#   INDICATIVE ONLY.
#   the DIFFERENCES rest on 18 pairs across 5 elements and are what A1's
#   field shift actually consumes. USABLE, with the stated error.
# *** AND THEY WERE NOT NEEDED (R 1562). A1's test uses the THEORETICAL KL3
# *** column, which for Bk and Cf already encodes an assumed radius — so
# *** testing these predictions against it is circular. The experimental
# *** column has errors of 0.2-15 eV against shifts of 0.6-2.2 eV and gives
# *** ratios of -14.7, -14.1 and 181.9. The four MEASURED anchors establish
# *** the proportionality at r = +0.916 with 12% scatter; adding these two
# *** moves the slope 13.5% and does not sharpen it.
# *** KEEP THEM as a record of the method (R 1561), not as A1 input.
